topics.name: Words used as nouns and verbs

options: The letter was sent by Ramanujan.
The letter was send by Ramanujan.
The letter were sent by Ramanujan.
questions.rule: Passive = was/were + past participle. One letter: was sent.

options: Our class paid a visiting to the science museum.
Our class paid a visits to the science museum.
Our class paid a visit to the science museum.
questions.rule: Here visit is a noun: a visit (singular after 'a').

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive needs the past participle: was decorated.
not only always pairs with but also.

questions.before: If you practise every day, you
questions.rule: Type 1: if + present, will + verb: If you practise, you will improve.
A compound sentence joins two main clauses with a coordinator like but.

chat: Who wrote this letter to Hardy?
questions.rule: Passive: was + past participle. The participle of write is written.

chat: Can you help me with the maths puzzle this evening?
options: Sure, if Mum will let me go out, I help you.
Sure, if Mum lets me go out, I helped you.
Sure, if Mum lets me go out, I will help you.
questions.rule: Type 1: present tense after if, will in the main clause.
Simple past active becomes was/were + past participle: was taught.

questions.source: Hardy was bored by that manuscript.
questions.rule: The doer (the manuscript) becomes the subject; keep the past tense: bored.

options: Asha likes maths, but her brother like music.
Asha likes maths, but her brother liking music.
Asha likes maths, but her brother likes music.
questions.rule: Each clause of a compound sentence needs its own correct verb: her brother likes.

options: Hardy wrote a report on the new theorems.
Hardy wrote a reported on the new theorems.
Hardy wrote report on the new theorems.
questions.rule: Here report is a noun, so it needs an article: a report.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After to use the base form of the verb: to watch.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After will use the base form: will stay.

questions.after: a Fellow of the Royal Society at thirty.
questions.rule: The Society elected him, so he was elected (passive).
After a big we need a noun: a big surprise.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the passive voice.
questions.rule: Plural subject: were checked, then by + the doer.

chat: How did the team do in the maths quiz?
options: They not only won but also set a record.
They not only won but also sets a record.
They not only won but set also a record.
questions.rule: Both parts match in tense: not only won but also set (past of set is set).

questions.source: Ravi finished his sums. He went out to play.
options: Ravi finished his sums and goes out to play.
Ravi finished his sums and went out to played.
Ravi finished his sums and went out to play.
questions.rule: Keep both verbs in the past: finished ... and went. After to, the base form: play.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: was given, was checked.

options: The boy which solved the puzzle is my classmate.
The boy who solved the puzzle are my classmate.
The boy who solved the puzzle is my classmate.
questions.rule: A person takes who; the main subject 'the boy' is singular, so is.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: not only ... but also is a fixed pair.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Type 2 (imaginary): If I were ... I would + verb.

questions.before: Ravi could not play in the final
questions.rule: A full clause (he had hurt his knee) follows because; 'because of' takes only a noun.
The clause that was lost describes the book, so it comes right after it.

chat: What would you do if you won a lot of money?
options: I would buying a telescope for our school.
I would bought a telescope for our school.
I would buy a telescope for our school.
questions.rule: An imaginary situation (type 2) is answered with would + base verb: would buy.

chat: Did you watch the final yesterday?
options: Yes, I watch it with my cousins yesterday.
Yes, I watched it with my cousins.
Yes, I did watched it with my cousins.
questions.rule: Here watch is a verb in the past: watched. After 'did' we would need the base form.

questions.source: Sheets of paper were found in it by Hardy.
options: Hardy found sheets of paper in it.
Hardy finds sheets of paper in it.
Hardy was found sheets of paper in it.
questions.rule: Passive past were found becomes active past found, with Hardy as subject.

questions.prompt: Change into a complex sentence using 'when'.
questions.source: Hardy opened the envelope and found sheets of symbols.
options: When Hardy opened the envelope, he finds sheets of symbols.
When Hardy opened the envelope, he found sheets of symbols.
When Hardy opened the envelope, and he found sheets of symbols.
questions.rule: When makes one clause dependent, so drop 'and' and keep the past tense.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Both Aman and Divya are two people, so come; not only pairs with but also.

options: Ramanujan's notebooks has been studied by many mathematicians.
Ramanujan's notebooks have been studied by many mathematicians.
Ramanujan's notebooks have been study by many mathematicians.
questions.rule: Plural subject + present perfect passive: have been studied.

options: If our school had a telescope, we will watch the stars every night.
If our school has a telescope, we would watch the stars every night.
If our school had a telescope, we would watch the stars every night.
questions.rule: Type 2: if + past, would + verb. Do not mix had with will, or has with would.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Here surprise is a verb in a past story: the dream surprised everyone.
Modal passive: could not be + past participle.
After paid (someone) we need a noun with its article: a visit.
A general truth: if + present, present.

chat: Has the result of the quiz been announced?
options: Yes, it has announced an hour ago.
Yes, it has been announced an hour ago.
Yes, it was announced an hour ago.
questions.rule: An hour ago is a finished time, so use the simple past passive: was announced.

questions.source: The principal will felicitate the quiz winner.
options: The quiz winner will felicitated by the principal.
The quiz winner will be felicitated by the principal.
The quiz winner would be felicitated by the principal.
questions.rule: Future passive: will be + past participle; keep 'will'.

questions.source: Ramanujan was a genius. He was very humble.
options: Ramanujan was not only a genius but also very humble.
Ramanujan was not only a genius and also very humble.
Ramanujan was not only a genius but also very humbly.
questions.rule: Use but also, and after 'was' we need the adjective humble.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Match the past: loved ... filled; passive are studied; 1918 is past, so he was thirty.

options: Ramanujan, who was largely self-taught, elected a Fellow at thirty.
Ramanujan, who was largely self-taught, was elected a Fellow at thirty.
Ramanujan, who were largely self-taught, was elected a Fellow at thirty.
questions.rule: Others elected him, so the main verb is passive: was elected; 'who' refers to one man: was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive: is known (past participle of know).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Type 2: would + base form: would send.

questions.after: Ramanujan elected a Fellow of the Royal Society, but he was also made a Fellow of Trinity.
questions.rule: When a sentence begins with Not only, the helper comes before the subject: was Ramanujan elected (passive).
Modal perfect passive: must have been + past participle.

chat: I don't understand this theorem at all.
options: If I was you, I will ask Ms Kulkarni for help.
If I were you, I would asked Ms Kulkarni for help.
If I were you, I would ask Ms Kulkarni for help.
questions.rule: Advice with type 2: If I were you, I would + base verb.

chat: Why was Hardy irritated by the letter at first?
options: Because it had no proofs and it look like a fraud.
Because it had not proofs and it looked like a fraud.
Because it had no proofs and it looked like a fraud.
questions.rule: Both joined clauses stay in the past (had ... looked); before a noun use no, not 'not'.

options: By whom was this strange letter send?
By whom this strange letter was sent?
By whom was this strange letter sent?
questions.rule: Who becomes By whom; keep question order: was + subject + sent.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Past story: earned; one person: was sent; passive: was recognised.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Passive: will be given; after will use the base verb: will watch.
